The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat fusion) achieves 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (instead of concat) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is the best next step as it builds on the current multimodal/singleprofile setup, explores a key design choice (fusion method), and avoids changing multiple parameters simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 have moderate performance. This experiment tests multiprofile with the same encoders but avgpool aggregation, clarifying whether multiprofile improves performance and isolating the effect of aggregation. It balances exploration of key design choices (profile setting) with minimal changes to other parameters.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings (config_018) significantly outperform singleprofile (0.6186 vs ~0.52). This experiment tests whether changing fusion from concat to weighted (while keeping multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, and avgpool aggregation) improves performance. It isolates the effect of fusion method in the promising multiprofile space, balancing exploitation of the current best configuration with exploration of key design choices.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (as in config_019) yield high performance. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated encoder) further improves accuracy, isolating the impact of RNA representation while maintaining the proven effective profile setting, aggregation, and fusion strategy.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and weighted fusion (e.g., config_031) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced model) further improves performance while keeping other components (scvi_n200 RNA encoder, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) consistent. This isolates the impact of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision, and builds on the strong foundation of the current top-performing configuration.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_037) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.7062). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (while retaining weighted fusion) improves performance, isolating the impact of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of the strong scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l combination with exploration of a potentially more effective aggregation strategy.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.724989). It balances exploitation of the current top-performing configuration with exploration of a critical design decision.
